Re-reviewed after the fix. Round 2 (kimi): rejected; repeats round 1 (afficit, debeatur, denominari, viribus, ordinis), and the round-1 fix passes glm.

Round 2 (kimi): rejected; 'without earning us any praise or reward' = 'ut non propterea laus, vel praemium ... debeatur' (propterea is the 'for it' of the result); 'does not make us good without qualification' = 'nec ab eo simpliciter boni denominemur'.

Re-reviewed after the fix. Round 2 (kimi+glm): rejected. glm: 'perfects nature' renders 'illam ... perficiunt' with the antecedent of illam (natura) named and the subject the advantages and gifts, as the English has it. kimi repeats the 'missing non' reading answered in round 1; 'apart from the character of virtue' = 'extra rationem virtutis'.

2222.resolution: Partly accepted. glm: 'in the same chapter 2' is now 'in the disputation cited above, chapter 2'. kimi's point on 'opponitur inevitabilitati' accepted in part: 'is an inevitability' paraphrased; now rendered literally 'is set against inevitability as to all sins together, not as to each', with a note on Tapper's sense, and 'nor is it a necessity of committing any particular sin' for 'nec est ad aliquod peccatum in specie committendum'. Rejected: 'There is no one who cannot refuse' = 'Nemo ... est qui non potest nolle' (everyone can refuse), as the Latin says; 'willing and refusing do not stay in our power' sits inside the 'ut non maneat' clause; 'the seventh of the Louvain articles' = 'ad articulum septimum Academiae Lovaniensis'; passive infinitives rendered with the same sense. Re-reviewed after the fix. Round 2 (kimi+glm): glm accepted: now 'on the seventh article of the Academy of Louvain'; kimi's 'non parum' point accepted: 'fairly common' is now 'quite common'. Rejected again: 'who cannot refuse' (= 'qui non potest nolle'; everyone can refuse); 'do not stay in our power' inside 'ut non maneat'; the passive infinitives keep the same sense; 'writers' for 'recentioribus' names the persons meant. English entry patched after append. Round 3 (kimi): one point accepted: 'and so avoid' for '& etiam vitare' added a consequence the Latin lacks; now 'and even avoid'. Rejected: passive 'servari/vinci' (same sense); 'strong' for 'vehementem' (near-synonym); 'as to all sins together' for 'quoad universa' (the context is sins; note explains); 'nor is it a necessity of committing' (necessitas is understood from the previous clause); 'reports' for 'testatur'. Round 4 (kimi, after the 'and even avoid' fix): all rejected, no change. Passive 'servari/vinci' (same sense); 'without grace' for 'gratia destituti'; 'who cannot refuse' (Nemo est qui non potest nolle: everyone can refuse) and 'ut non maneat' (result clause) are read correctly, and the model misreads both again; 'make it necessary to follow it' for 'inducere necessitatem ipsam sequendi' ('ipsam' = the passion); 'all sins together' for 'quoad universa'; 'a necessity of committing' carries 'necessitas' from the clause before; 'reports' for 'testatur'; 'quite common' renders the litotes 'non parum' (the model's own round-2 point).
